pointers.sentence: A **migration**, as the loader makes it, is an instance of the class `Migration` that a migration file defines, a subclass of the `Migration` of `django.db.migrations` (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration`).

`django.db.migrations` imports the base class, `swappable_dependency` and the operation classes that `django.db.migrations.operations` exports, so a file reaches them all as attributes of one package (`django/db/migrations/__init__.py`).
`Migration` gives each of its attributes a value, so the subclass that a migration file defines need state only those that differ (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration`).

A key in `run_before` names one that must be applied after: this migration's node becomes a parent of that one's, as if the other file had named this migration in its own `dependencies` (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.add_internal_dependencies`, `django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.add_external_dependencies`; [The migration graph: `MigrationGraph`](graph.md)).

A key in `run_before` names one that must be applied after: this migration's node becomes a parent of that one's, as if the other file had named this migration in its own `dependencies` (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.add_internal_dependencies`, `django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.add_external_dependencies`; [The migration graph: `MigrationGraph`](graph.md)).

The autodetector sets `initial` on each migration it makes, to true where the application has no model in the state the migration files make (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._build_migration_list`), and the writer writes `initial = True` for a true value and nothing for any other ([Writing a migration file: `MigrationWriter`](../makemigrations/writer.md)).

`Migration.__init__` keeps the name and the label, and gives the instance its own copy of each list of the class: the operations, the dependencies, `Migration.run_before` and `Migration.replaces` (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.__init__`).

Its comment gives the reason, that the lists may be changed at runtime, and they are: `makemigrations --update` extends the operations and the dependencies of a migration the loader made (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.write_to_last_migration_files`; [Rewriting migrations: `--update`, squashmigrations and optimizemigration](../makemigrations/rewriting.md)).

Two migrations are equal when their names and their labels are equal, whatever else they hold, and a migration's hash is that of the string `str` makes of it, the label and the name with a dot between: migrations can be kept in a set and be the keys of a dict, as the executor keeps them (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.__eq__`, `django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.__hash__`).

`Migration.mutate_state` runs the state half of each operation in order, on one project state, and returns that state (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.mutate_state`).

For each operation in turn it clones the state, runs the state half on the state it was given, and calls the database half forwards with the clone as the from-state and the state as the to-state (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.apply`).

`Migration.apply` and `Migration.unapply` add a block only where the editor has none: an operation's database half then runs in an atomic block of its own when `Operation.atomic` is true, or when it is anything but `False` and `Migration.atomic` is true (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.apply`, `django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation`).

`Migration.apply` and `Migration.unapply` add a block only where the editor has none: an operation's database half then runs in an atomic block of its own when `Operation.atomic` is true, or when it is anything but `False` and `Migration.atomic` is true (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.apply`, `django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation`).

`Migration.unapply` is given what `Migration.apply` is given, the state before the migration, and has to call each operation's database half backwards, last operation first, each with the state after its operation as the from-state and the state before it as the to-state (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.unapply`).

The first pass begins each turn by reading `Operation.reversible`, and raises `IrreversibleError`, a `RuntimeError`, at the first operation for which it is false (`django/db/migrations/exceptions.py:IrreversibleError`, `django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation`).

`MigrationLoader.collect_sql` calls them so, and sqlmigrate prints the result (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.apply`, `django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.collect_sql`; [The migrate command, showmigrations and sqlmigrate](migrate.md)).

`MigrationLoader.collect_sql` calls them so, and sqlmigrate prints the result (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.apply`, `django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.collect_sql`; [The migrate command, showmigrations and sqlmigrate](migrate.md)).
After any other operation it appends `"-- (no-op)"` if the database half added nothing to the list (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation`).

Where no `--name` was given, `MigrationAutodetector.arrange_for_graph` asks it for each new migration that is not its application's first, and `makemigrations --update` for the one it rewrites (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.suggest_name`; [From operations to migrations: dependencies, order and names](../makemigrations/dependencies.md)).

Otherwise it takes each operation's `Operation.migration_name_fragment`, with every run of characters other than letters, digits and underscores made an underscore (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation`).

`swappable_dependency` is given the setting's value as the file is imported, and returns the label that value begins with, paired with `"__first__"`, as a `SwappableTuple`: a tuple that also carries the value it was made from (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:swappable_dependency`).

Squashmigrations reads the value the tuple carries: where that is the current value of `AUTH_USER_MODEL`, the file it writes has the call again (`django/core/management/commands/squashmigrations.py:Command.handle`; [Rewriting migrations: `--update`, squashmigrations and optimizemigration](../makemigrations/rewriting.md)).
